holidays.name: National Ride the Wind Day
holidays.description: A day for catching a breeze and going with the flow. Fly a kite, hoist a sail, cruise with the windows down, or just stand on a hilltop and let your hair get wild. Whatever the wind is doing, you get to play along.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a staple on fun-holiday calendars as a nudge to get outside and enjoy the air.
holidays.funFact: The Beaufort scale, created in 1805, rates wind from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane force). It was originally based on how much sail a ship could carry.

holidays.name: Buttered Corn Day
holidays.description: A celebration of sweet summer corn on the cob, dripping with melted butter. It falls in peak corn season, so grab a cob, a stick of butter and plenty of napkins. Chin-glistening is encouraged.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It lands in late August, when sweet corn is at its best across much of North America.
holidays.funFact: An ear of corn almost always has an even number of kernel rows, usually 16, and each strand of silk is attached to one potential kernel.

holidays.name: Internaut Day
holidays.description: A tip of the hat to the pioneers of the internet and everyone who surfs, scrolls and clicks their way through it. It's a good day to remember the weird, wonderful early web, so go ahead and bookmark something delightful.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is widely listed as a nod to people who explore the online world, which is where the word 'Internaut' comes from.
holidays.funFact: 'Internaut' blends 'Internet' and 'astronaut', much like 'cybernaut'. Both words came from the idea of explorers navigating a new digital frontier.
